# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 55

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 11

---

## Disagreement 1 — 55:1 "well-regarded" vs. "well-esteemed" vs. "well-regarded"

- **EMET:** "trustworthy and well-regarded"
- **LOGOS:** "trustworthy and well-esteemed"
- **PNEUMA:** "reliable, well-regarded"
- **Greek:** *pistos kai endoxos* — faithful/trustworthy and honorable/esteemed
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "trustworthy and well-esteemed" (LOGOS). *Endoxos* = held in honor/esteemed; "well-esteemed" is slightly more elevated than "well-regarded."

---

## Disagreement 2 — 55:1 "fence it around" vs. "fence the vineyard" — precision

- **EMET:** "gave him the vineyard to fence it around"
- **LOGOS:** "giving him this charge: fence the vineyard"
- **PNEUMA:** "He gave this slave one instruction: fence the vineyard in"
- **Greek:** *phraxon ton ampelōna* — fence the vineyard
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "giving him this charge: fence the vineyard, and nothing more" (LOGOS). The "nothing more" (*kai mēden allo*) is critical — it defines the limit of the command. EMET omits it from the summary.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 55:1 "free in my house" vs. "free in my household"

- **EMET:** "you shall be free in my house"
- **LOGOS:** "you shall be free in my household"
- **PNEUMA:** "you'll have your freedom in my household"
- **Greek:** *eleutheros esē en tō oikō mou* — you shall be free in my house/household
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "you shall be free in my household" (LOGOS). "Household" captures the social/economic unit better than "house" (physical structure).

---

## Disagreement 4 — 55:2 "went away to a foreign country" vs. "went away abroad"

- **EMET:** "went away to a foreign country"
- **LOGOS:** "went away abroad"
- **PNEUMA:** "went abroad"
- **Greek:** *apedēmēsen eis xenēn chōran* — went away to a foreign land
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "went away abroad" (LOGOS). "Abroad" is economical; "foreign country" (EMET) is accurate but verbose.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 55:3 "reasoned within himself" vs. "deliberated within himself"

- **EMET:** "he reasoned within himself"
- **LOGOS:** "he deliberated within himself"
- **PNEUMA:** "He thought it over"
- **Greek:** *dielogizeto en heautō* — deliberated/reasoned with himself
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "he deliberated within himself" (LOGOS). *Dialogizomai* = to deliberate/reason through; "deliberated" captures the careful inner reasoning.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 55:3 "more beautiful when it is dug" vs. "more attractive"

- **EMET:** "it shall be more beautiful when it is dug"
- **LOGOS:** "when it is dug it will be more attractive"
- **PNEUMA:** "it'll be much more attractive"
- **Greek:** *kalos estin kan* — it will be beautiful/fine
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "when it is dug it will be more attractive" (LOGOS). "Attractive" captures the visual improvement; "beautiful" (EMET) is acceptable but less precise for agricultural context.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 55:4 "friends who were his counselors" vs. "friends who were his advisors"

- **EMET:** "friends who were his counselors"
- **LOGOS:** "friends who were his advisors"
- **PNEUMA:** "closest advisors"
- **Greek:** *tous philous autou tous symboulous* — his friends who were his counselors/advisors
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "his friends who were his advisors" (LOGOS). "Advisors" is slightly more contemporary; "counselors" (EMET) is formal but not wrong; PNEUMA loses "friends."

---

## Disagreement 8 — 55:5 "joint heir" vs. "co-heir"

- **EMET:** "make him joint heir with my son"
- **LOGOS:** "make him co-heir with my son"
- **PNEUMA:** "make him a co-heir with my son"
- **Greek:** *synklēronomon tou huiou mou* — co-heir/joint heir with my son
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "make him co-heir with my son" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). "Co-heir" is the standard NT translation of *synklēronomi* (Rom 8:17; Eph 3:6); "joint heir" (EMET) is acceptable but less standard.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 55:5 "carried it out" vs. "carried it through"

- **EMET:** "he did not neglect it but carried it out"
- **LOGOS:** "he did not neglect it but carried it through"
- **PNEUMA:** "he didn't ignore it — he acted on it"
- **Greek:** *ouk ēmelēsen alla epeteles* — did not neglect but completed/accomplished
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "he did not neglect it but carried it through" (LOGOS). "Carried it through" implies completion of the whole project; "carried it out" is slightly less emphatic.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 55:6 "beloved son" — all agree

- **EMET:** "master's son agreed"
- **LOGOS:** "master's son concurred"
- **PNEUMA:** "master's son agreed"
- **Greek:** *synēudokēsen ho huios autou* — the son agreed/consented
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "master's son concurred" (LOGOS). "Concurred" is slightly more formal and appropriate to a legal/inheritance decision.

---

## Disagreement 11 — 55:7 "goodness of his heart" vs. "generosity of his heart"

- **EMET:** "goodness of his heart"
- **LOGOS:** "generosity of his heart"
- **PNEUMA:** "the generosity behind them"
- **Greek:** *tēs agathosunēs tēs kardias autou* — the goodness/generosity of his heart
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the generosity of his heart" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). *Agathosunē* = goodness; in context the specific form of goodness is generosity — LOGOS's "generosity" is a legitimate contextual rendering.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 55.*
